prompt:
You are a decision-support tool for a radiologist. Review this patient's frontal chest X-ray and report on six findings. A radiologist checks your output; give your best assessment. Findings and their definitions: - Lung Opacity: airspace opacity, consolidation, infiltrate or airspace disease in the lung. A discrete nodule or mass is not Lung Opacity (it is Lung Lesion). - Cardiomegaly: an enlarged heart. A borderline or upper-normal heart size counts as absent. - Atelectasis: collapse or incomplete expansion of lung tissue, including subsegmental or plate-like atelectasis. - Lung Lesion: a nodule, mass or cavity in the lung. A calcified granuloma does not count. - Pleural Effusion: fluid in the pleural space. - Fracture: a fracture of the ribs, clavicles, spine or any other visible bone. Healed or old fractures count. How to work: 1. Read the patient's image systematically first. 2. Then look at the 10 most similar cases from a reference database, listed below with their reports. They are other patients whose images look similar to this one. Use them as supporting evidence to confirm or question what you see in the patient's image, not as the answer: a finding in a similar case does not mean that this patient has it. 3. For each of the six findings, give its status (present, absent or uncertain), the probability (0 to 1) that it is present in this patient, the IDs of the similar cases that support your call (an empty list if none), and a rationale of one or two sentences. Then give a short impression. Do not explain what the findings are. Cite cases by their ID exactly as written, e.g. CXR316. Give the probability with two decimals as your honest estimate; for subtle, borderline or partly obscured appearances, use intermediate values rather than a fixed low value. Similar cases (most similar first): Case CXR1719 (similarity 0.978): FINDINGS: The cardiomediastinal silhouette is within normal limits for size. Pulmonary vasculature is within normal limits. No focal consolidations, effusions, or pneumothoraces. No acute bony abnormality. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality. Case CXR1005 (similarity 0.975): FINDINGS: Cardiac and mediastinal contours are within normal limits. The lungs are clear. Bony structures are intact. IMPRESSION: No acute findings. Case CXR2192 (similarity 0.972): FINDINGS: No focal lung consolidation. No pneumothorax or pleural effusion.Heart size and pulmonary vascularity are within normal limits.Minimal degenerative changes of the thoracic spine. The previously
described XXXX deformity in the midthoracic spine is again seen. There is subcutaneous shunt catheter tubing along the anterior chest wall IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary process. Case CXR3575 (similarity 0.972): FINDINGS: Heart size normal. No pneumothorax, pleural effusion, or focal airspace disease. Central left midlung granuloma with calcified left hilar adenopathy. Bony structures appear intact. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality. Case CXR2147 (similarity 0.971): FINDINGS: Cardiac and mediastinal contours are within normal limits. The lungs are clear. Mild spondylosis. IMPRESSION: No acute findings. Case CXR1689 (similarity 0.970): FINDINGS: Heart size and mediastinal contours appear within normal limits. Pulmonary vascularity is within normal limits. No focal consolidation, suspicious pulmonary opacity, pneumothorax or definite pleural effusion. Visualized osseous structures appear intact. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality. Case CXR832 (similarity 0.970): IMPRESSION: Heart normal. Lungs clear. Calcified left lower lobe 5 mm granuloma Case CXR623 (similarity 0.969): FINDINGS: The heart is normal in size. The mediastinum is stable. Atherosclerotic calcifications of the aorta. There is again a pleural based density in the right lung base, XXXX related to subpleural fat. The appearance is stable from multiple previous studies. The lungs are clear. There is no pleural effusion. IMPRESSION: No acute disease. Case CXR2029 (similarity 0.969): FINDINGS: Normal heart size and mediastinal contours. No focal airspace consolidation. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. The visualized osseous structures are unremarkable in appearance. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary abnormalities. Case CXR3112 (similarity 0.969): FINDINGS: The heart is normal in size. The mediastinum is unremarkable. The lungs are clear. IMPRESSION: No acute disease. The patient's frontal chest X-ray follows.
